test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: general
question:
The circumference of the base of a cylindrical vessel is 264 cm and its height is 50 cm. The capacity (in litres) of the vessel is:

(Take π = (22)/(7))
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume of cylinder is proportional to π, so check for divisibility by 11 in the options.

Radius (r) = Circumference ÷ (2 × π) = 264 ÷ (2 × 22/7) = 42 cm.

Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × 42 × 42 × 50 = 277200 cm³.

Capacity = 277200 ÷ 1000 = 277.2 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 277.2 litres.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Circumference of the base = 264 cm

Height (h) of the vessel = 50 cm

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Circumference = 2 × π × r

Volume of Cylinder = π × r² × h

1 litre = 1000 cm³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e2dac19f2d342c5230f74bf671dec61e804bdda3cc1b900418f68e495a56c65c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 264

⇒ (44/7) × r = 264

⇒ r = (264 × 7) ÷ 44

⇒ r = 6 × 7 = 42 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 42 × 42 × 50

⇒ Volume = 22 × 6 × 42 × 50

⇒ Volume = 132 × 2100 = 277200 cm³

⇒ Capacity in litres = 277200 ÷ 1000

⇒ Capacity = 277.2 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 277.2 litres.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The volume or capacity of a cylinder is given by the formula V = πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved surface of a cylinder is CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area including the top and bottom circles is TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Unit Conversions

Common units include 1 cm³ = 1 mL, 1000 cm³ = 1 litre, and 1 m³ = 1000 litres.</p
